Q23.1: Do not live in a suburb. Live in a rural area in South Australia. I am retired. Work questions were not applicable but no not applicable option.  South Australia has had few covid cases and very few deaths. It is recommended to keep 1.5 metres apart not 2. Community events have had to be cancelled because of covid and travel was restricted for a while. Can go shopping, exercising, out for a meal, etc but 4 square metres per person is recommended. Kept cooking at Meals on wheels kitchen. Have only had to wear a mask there once and shopping once. Bad news with glasses. Well done to people who have had to wear them frequently. Point is restrictions and experiences around the world have varied but the survey has no allowance for that. People at most risk of catching and spreading covid should get vaccinated 1st. Protecting communities means high numbers of people have to be vaccinated. I was a teacher and caught whooping cough presumably from my workplace and learnt immunisation wears off. Staff of a similar age and I were all immunised again. Vaccinations work and are preferable to the conditions. How strong is the risk of another pandemic after this one? I read an interesting article in American scientific magazine saying the more land that is cleared, the more himans and wild animals cohabitate an area the higher the risk of more pandemics. Re travel - not interested in going overseas again except maybe New Zealand for years if ever. Re income - have lost income since am a self funded retiree and super balances were badly hit and government recommended halving pension payments to reduce the impact of covid. No government support available or sought. Just spend less, do less. Vaccinations need to be done throughout the world and areas of major risk 1st. Wealthy countries will have to help. Not sure how much so that was a tough question to try and answer. More thought was needed in designing the survey to allow for people in different circumstances.
